doc.title: Carol Bash interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2012

title: Her own gear and the need for an editor and outside eyes
summary: Bash owns a basic camera and lighting kit and Final Cut, but relies on a professional editor and outside eyes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Now do you own your own gear?
To some extent? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-

Um hum. I have a basic camera. I have a SONY pd 150, you know it’s out of date now, it’s a mini-dv camera. And I have a very basic lighting kit. Because I mean I can shoot, I can compose a shot, and quite honestly, in those situations, in this documentary there were times when I didn’t have the money and yet I wanted to interview somebody, whether they were moving on in years or they were in a location that I could get to. So I shot, you know, with my pd 150 and my basic lighting kit and, you know, it works. But believe me, when I have the money to pay for a professional, I pay for a professional, absolutely.

Some things have gotten cheaper, I mean less expensive. Like you probably do, do you have an editing machine or a suite or something, instead of paying a company three or four hundred dollars an hour?

Well you know that’s the other thing. I mean yes, I have Final Cut Pro on my laptop, you know, but I’m not an editor. Again, editing is a craft. I have an editor who’s fantastic. And what she does, and how she paces out the visual and the audio and creates a mood through the materials is something that I couldn’t do. It’s really a craft. She went through the channels of apprenticeship and sitting at the heels of well-known editors, I mean she has been doing this for decades. So I’m not going to presume that I could come in there, even if I have the software, that I’d be able to edit like that.
That is a danger. Too many people have the toys now and they think that, yeah, I can make a record now because I have the —

And there’s nothing wrong with doing it yourself. But I think you have to be humble in that process. You know I do think you can’t do it all yourself. I think a film suffers if you’re doing everything. You really do need outside eyes to sort of help you with the materials. Because you can’t see objectively. And yeah, but sometimes, it calls for, as I said, the financing’s not there and you’ve got to go out there and shoot or you don’t have the money and you can edit, you know, you’ve got to do what you’ve got to do. But I totally agree that the best way is to just get somebody who really has that real fine sense of craft to help you with your film.
